pure-announcement.rationale: Standing documentation of a long-lived OSS tool, not a launch or release note, and it carries a transferable practice: generate uniform SLO recording and burn-rate alert rules from a compact spec instead of hand-writing them per team.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concept 'SLO burn-rate alerting' covers the Workbook technique itself; a reader of it still learns the generation layer here — spec-to-rules compilation, CI validation, Kubernetes CRD mode, OpenSLO interop — so this is operationalization, not restatement.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The generator's behavior is checkable end-to-end: the note links both the example spec and the exact generated rules file in the public repo.

durability.rationale: Sloth is a years-established generator whose core mechanism — compile a small SLO spec into recording rules plus multiwindow multi-burn alerts — has been stable across releases and will almost certainly still hold in twelve months, with only badge versions as perishable trim.

actionability.rationale: The concrete steps are product-bound (sloth generate, validate, operator mode); the transferable decision — prefer spec-driven generation over hand-written burn-rate rules — is stated only as a one-line uniformity claim.

atomicity.rationale: One idea end to end — a spec-to-rules SLO generator built on the Google SRE alerting framework — statable in a single paragraph without the feature list.
